subject: CSR timestamping, delegated-issuer audit & operator playbook
messages:
From: FinAcuity Audit Team <audit@finacuity.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Evidence request: CSR timeline & delegated issuer audit

Hi Kimberly / Marissa,

As part of our compliance review for the upcoming regulatory audit, we need a verifiable timeline and proof for all CSRs and certificates issued to our private endpoints on your private deployment (VPC) since 2025-06-01. In particular we need:

- Raw CSR blobs (or a tamper-evident export) with exact submit timestamps
- Proof of the signing issuer for each certificate (indication if a delegated subordinate CA was used)
- Timestamping / RFC3161 evidence that ties the CSR/issue event to a wall-clock time
- Chain of custody: operator who requested, operator who approved, and KMS/HSM reference used to sign

Please attach any artifacts you can provide (checksums preferred) and a short description of your operator playbook for CSR issuance and delegated-issuer rotation. We have the questionnaire attached with the sections highlighted that are relevant to this ask.

Deliverable deadline: Can you provide initial artifacts by EOD 2025-07-23? If not, propose a date and we'll schedule a short sync.

Thanks,
Aditi Kaul
FinAcuity Audit Team

Attachment: FinAcuity_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: FinAcuity Audit Team <audit@finacuity.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2025-07-19T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: CSR timeline & delegated issuer audit

Hi Aditi,

Thanks for the clear list. We can provide the artifacts you requested — our plan is to produce a tamper-evident export and an operator-level playbook that documents the issuance flow, approvals, and KMS references. Quick summary of what we'll deliver by the EOD 2025-07-23 target: 

- csr_bundle_20250719.tar.gz: raw CSR files, associated RFC3161 timestamps, and SHA256 checksums
- mapping.csv: certificate serial -> tenant_id -> operator_id -> KMS_key_id
- operator_playbook.md: step-by-step for CSR submission, approval gates, and delegated-issuer usage
- issuer_rotation_checklist.md: how we rotate subordinate issuers and preserve continuity for OCSP/CT

A few clarifying asks so we tailor the artifacts correctly:
1) Do you need the RFC3161 timestamp token itself or is an HSM-signed timestamp + hash sufficient?
2) For delegated issuers, do you need full subordinate CA private-key custody proofs (we do not expose private keys) or do you accept HSM key IDs and audit logs showing signing events?

CC'ing Jonas for the operational/technical details and Marissa for compliance coordination. We'll produce the archive and a short README that explains the fields and correlation IDs.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

Attachment: csr_bundle_20250719.tar.gz (tar.gz)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2025-07-20T08:33:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evidence request: CSR timeline & delegated issuer audit

Kim / Jonas —

I sketched an operator playbook (high level) we can include in operator_playbook.md. Please review and propose edits: 

Operator playbook (high level):
1) CSR generation: tenant creates CSR via our private onboarding API or operator-run portal. Save raw CSR as PEM and capture submit timestamp (UTC) from API gateway.
2) Pre-approval hook: automated policy check (hostname assertions, tenant contract checks). If policy passes, assign correlation_id and enqueue for signing.
3) Signing: sign action is performed by the CA service which calls KMS/HSM to sign the certificate or delegate to subordinate CA. For each sign event we store:
   - CSR SHA256, API correlation_id, operator_id, KMS_key_id, signing_method (direct|delegated-subordinate), and RFC3161 timestamp token (where available)
4) Timestamping: we will record an RFC3161 timestamp for the CSR or the final certificate. If external RFC3161 TSA is required for evidentiary purposes we can attach that token to the bundle.
5) Storage: write all artifacts to WORM (object store with immutability flag) with checksum and index the artifact in our audit index (immutable event store).
6) Rotation/Revocation: when rotating subordinate issuers we produce a continuity manifest that maps old->new serial ranges and publishes CT and OCSP responder updates to ensure in-flight validation for clients.

Operator deliverables for the archive: 
- RAW_CSRs/ (PEM files)
- RFC3161_TOKENS/ (if used)
- SIGN_EVENTS.csv (CSR_SHA256, cert_serial, correlation_id, operator_id, kms_key_id, timestamp)
- CONTINUITY_MANIFEST.json (old_issuer, new_issuer, cutover_time_utc)

If that aligns with what you need, I'll prepare the bundle and README.

Marissa
Sr. Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

(Internal note: Jonas, we need a small script to export SIGN_EVENTS.csv from the events DB and a job to push RFC3161 tokens into the WORM store.)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2025-07-21T10:17:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Operator playbook + technical details for RFC3161 / delegated issuer

Thanks — technical clarifications below (for the README and the audit bundle):

- RFC3161: We currently support two modes: internal timestamping via our HSM-backed RFC3161 service (preferred for speed) and an optional external TSA (proof for legal third parties). The timestamp token (TST) will be included alongside the CSR PEM as TST_<csr_sha256>.rfc3161.
- Delegated subordinate CA: We will not export private keys. Proof of delegation provided will include: subordinate CA certificate, signed delegation policy, KMS_key_id that performed the sign operation, and an immutable signing event record with a trace-id.
- OCSP/Stapling: For short-lived certs we staple OCSP responses from the responder tied to the subordinate issuer. OCSP responses are stored in the audit store with responder serial and nextUpdate timestamp.
- Audit correlation: use a single correlation_id per issuance flow that surfaces in API gateway logs, CA service logs, and KMS audit logs. We'll include a small export tool: export_sign_events.sh which produces SIGN_EVENTS.csv and a provenance.log (human readable timeline).
- Evidence integrity: all exported artifacts will be signed with a per-tenant export key (export_key_id) and we will publish SHA256 checksums in the README. The export itself will be timestamped (RFC3161) to attestate the time of export.

I'll attach issuer_rotation_checklist.md (internal checklist) and schedule a 30-minute runbook review with SRE to validate the WORM export and the RFC3161 embedding. Proposed runbook review: 2025-07-22 14:00 PDT.

Jonas
Staff Infra Engineer — Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Attachment: issuer_rotation_checklist.md (text/markdown)

From: FinAcuity Audit Team <audit@finacuity.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Date: 2025-07-23T16:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CSR timestamping, delegated-issuer audit & operator playbook

Kim, Marissa, Jonas —

Thanks — this level of detail is exactly what we were after. A few quick follow-ups: 

- Please include the RFC3161 TST tokens where possible; if you use internal HSM RFC3161 tokens, include the HSM key identifiers and the signing event IDs.
- For delegated subordinate CAs, we accept the subordinate cert + signed delegation policy + KMS audit events — no private keys needed.
- We'll take the download and check checksums. If everything verifies we'll sign off on the evidence package.

Can we have the bundle and a short README before the runbook review? If you can get the artifacts to us by 2025-07-23 20:00 PDT we will validate them and join the 07-22 runbook review time if it's shifted to the 22nd; otherwise propose a runbook time on the 23rd morning.

Meeting request: I've attached a DocuSign pre-auth for the evidence exchange agreement; please sign and we'll proceed.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

— Aditi
FinAcuity Audit Team
